spec.title: The own checker's encoding timed whole per word-level operation: the benchmark's own-checker runs, flagged phasesExcess and time against job 20261106-201041
spec.description: The own checker (lib/src/bmc/bits.rs) estimated its encoding phase by timing one in 64 operations at random and counting it 64 times over. Single gates (nanoseconds) and whole word-level circuits (a 32-bit multiplier is thousands of gates) were sampled from the same stream, and the seed is fixed, so a short run that sampled one large circuit counted it 64 times on every run: its encoding plus solving passed the run's own time, and Phases::excess flagged it phasesExcess (1 of 356 own-checker runs in job 20261106-201041, real/checksum/broken-property under advised; example 018's proof in jobs -231837 and -000039). Now every word-level operation is timed whole, and only single gates are sampled. A new unit test (the_encoding_estimate_does_not_count_a_large_circuit_many_times_over) put one multiplication among 256 cheap gates at each position: before the change, at position 74 the encoding was estimated at 0.063 s of 0.001 s; after it, every position is within the phases' tolerance. This job reruns the benchmark's own-checker runs (all modes, no JBMC) at this commit, then checks that no run is flagged and that timing each word-level operation (two clock reads, about 0.6 us on WSL2) made the runs no slower than job -201041 measured on the same machine, by the median ratio of seconds over runs of 0.1 s or more. The committed lib/benchmark results are not rewritten: the run writes under lib/target.
spec.expected: exits 0: the benchmark runs, no own-checker run carries phasesExcess, and the median ratio of the own checker's seconds to job 20261106-201041's, over runs of 0.1 s or more, is at most 1.10. The second step prints the counts and the ratio's median and quartiles. A flagged run or a median above 1.10 is a finding to read, not a reason to change the tolerance.

steps.name: benchmark, own checker only
steps.run: (cd lib && cargo build --release -q) && python3 lib/benchmark/run.py --engines native --out lib/target/benchmark-native.json --table lib/target/benchmark-native.md

steps.name: compare with job 20261106-201041
steps.run:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, statistics, sys
new = [r for r in json.load(open("lib/target/benchmark-native.json"))["runs"] if r["engine"] == "native"]
old = {(r["case"], r["mode"]): r for r in json.load(open("lib/benchmark/results.json"))["runs"] if r["engine"] == "native"}
flagged = [(r["case"], r["mode"], r["phasesExcess"]) for r in new if r.get("phasesExcess")]
ratios = [r["seconds"] / old[(r["case"], r["mode"])]["seconds"] for r in new
          if (r["case"], r["mode"]) in old and old[(r["case"], r["mode"])]["seconds"] >= 0.1]
median = statistics.median(ratios)
print(f"own-checker runs: {len(new)}; flagged phasesExcess: {len(flagged)} (job 20261106-201041: 1 of 356)")
for f in flagged:
    print("  flagged:", *f)
print(f"seconds against job 20261106-201041, runs of 0.1 s or more: {len(ratios)}, median ratio {median:.3f}, "
      f"quartiles {statistics.quantiles(ratios, n=4)[0]:.3f} to {statistics.quantiles(ratios, n=4)[2]:.3f}")
sys.exit(0 if not flagged and median <= 1.10 else 1)
PY
